examGuide.title: Mental model and derivation
examGuide.body:
A variable is live when some future path reads its current value before redefining it. Liveness is a backward may analysis: successor OUT sets combine by union. IN=USE∪(OUT−DEF). An assignment may be dead if its defined value is not live afterward, but side effects can still prohibit deletion. Loop backedges must participate in fixed-point iteration, and self-use such as x=x+1 reads the old x.

**Key relationship:** OUT[B]=∪IN[successors]; IN[B]=USE[B]∪(OUT[B]−DEF[B])

examGuide.title: A repeatable solving procedure
examGuide.body:
1. Compute block USE and DEF carefully.
2. Propagate successor IN sets backward.
3. Iterate backedges and preserve side-effecting instructions.

examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: A variable is live if some future path uses its current value before redefining it. Solve backward with OUT=union of successor IN sets and IN=USE∪(OUT−DEF). Back edges can keep variables live across blocks even when the exit path uses nothing. Liveness supports dead-code removal and register interference analysis.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
Block contains x=a+b; y=x+c and exits where only y is live. How many variables are live at block entry?

**Answer: 3.** Work backward: before y=x+c, x and c are needed; before x=a+b, its old x is killed and a,b are needed. Entry set is {a,b,c}, of size 3. y's old value is not needed.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
An assignment can be removed only if its result is dead and evaluating it has no required side effects or exceptions under the chosen semantics.

Dead variable values and unreachable control-flow blocks are different forms of dead code.

examGuide.title: Worked question patterns
examGuide.body:
#### Pattern 1 · MCQ

For x=y+z, with OUT={x}, IN is:

- **A.** ∅
- **B.** {x}
- **C.** {y,z}
- **D.** {x,y,z}

**Answer: C.** USE={y,z},DEF={x}; IN=USE∪(OUT−DEF)={y,z}.

#### Pattern 2 · MSQ

Choose true statements.

- **A.** Liveness propagates only forward
- **B.** Successor paths combine by union
- **C.** A live variable must be read on every future path
- **D.** A dead assigned value does not automatically make side effects removable

**Answer: B, D.** Liveness is backward; successor possibilities combine by union. It is a may property needing some path, not all. Side effects still constrain deletion.

#### Pattern 3 · NAT

For a=b+c followed by return a, how many variables are live immediately before the assignment?



**Answer: 2.** b and c are needed to compute a. Old a is overwritten without reading, so precisely two variables are live.

examGuide.title: Work through the supplied PYQs
examGuide.body:
#### GATE 2023 CS · Q37 · MCQ

[Open the original question and try it](/#/lesson/liveness-analysis?tab=practice)

**What is tested:** Liveness analysis and dead code. Refer to the original image for complete givens and diagrams.

1. Use OUT(B)=union of successor IN sets, and IN(B)=USE(B)∪(OUT(B)−DEF(B)). The back edge B4→B2 matters even though B4 also reaches EXIT.
2. B2 uses old i,j and defines i,j; B3 defines a; B4 uses a and defines i. Iterating to a fixed point gives IN(B2)={a,i,j} and IN(B4)={a,j}.
3. Consequently OUT(B1)={a,i,j}, OUT(B2)={a,j}, OUT(B3)={a,j}, OUT(B4)={a,i,j}. Choose **D**.

#### GATE 2025 CS1 · Q13 · MCQ

[Open the original question and try it](/#/lesson/liveness-analysis?tab=practice)

**What is tested:** Liveness analysis and dead code. Refer to the original image for complete givens and diagrams.

1. Two variables whose values are simultaneously live cannot safely share the same register. Liveness intervals or an interference graph express these constraints.
2. Register allocation/assignment uses this information to reuse registers for nonoverlapping lifetimes and spill when necessary.
3. Hence **B**. Constant folding and strength reduction rely on different analyses; call management is not the listed allocation optimization.
